title: The Last Compass
premise: Gideon Okonkwo, once the most sought-after mountain guide on two continents, was blacklisted after an expedition that cost three lives and her reputation. When her old rival Mara Voss hires her crew for a forbidden crossing of the Karakoram passes to recover a dead climber's body and his father's lost compass, Gideon discovers the climber was her brother, presumed lost a decade ago. Betrayed by a crew member selling their route to smugglers, stranded by an early monsoon with a leaking boat on a glacial river, Gideon must accept help from Yusuf, a stranger with his own debts to the mountain. She reaches the ice cave where her brother died, learns he survived long enough to leave her the compass and a message of forgiveness, and returns not as a blacklisted guide but as the woman who finally stopped running from what she inherited: grief, guilt, and the will to lead again.
about_author: C. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent six years organizing high-altitude treks across Central Asia before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose pasts are harder terrain than any mountain.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Ten years after her blacklisting, she leads low-risk treks in Nepal, measuring life in distances covered. A letter arrives from Mara Voss offering a fortune for one job. Emotional beat: restless unease — the past has found her address.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Gideon meets Mara in Kathmandu. The job: retrieve a body and effects from a high pass, closed to expeditions since the disaster that ruined them both. Gideon refuses — until Mara says the dead man's name. Emotional beat: shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: The Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Gideon's POV. Ten years earlier: the expedition, the storm, the fall, and how her brother Emeka vanished into white while she led survivors down. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a body under moving ice.

chapters.title: Assembling the Crew
chapters.summary: Gideon recruits her small trusted team: old friend Bisi on ropes, skeptical medic Tomas, and quiet newcomer Dev, who knows the river valleys too well. Emotional beat: cautious hope shadowed by the sense that someone is watching.

chapters.title: Sworn Off Ground
chapters.summary: The crew crosses into restricted territory at night. Gideon navigates by memory of a route she swore never to walk again. First signs someone else is on the mountain. Emotional beat: dread braided with the strange comfort of returning.

chapters.title: What Dev Carries
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. He reveals fragments of why he joined: a debt, a brother of his own lost to the mountains. He photographs route notes 'for safety.' Emotional beat: sympathy for a man the reader begins to suspect.

chapters.title: The River That Shouldn't Run
chapters.summary: Glacial melt swells early; the planned crossing point is gone. They find an abandoned boat with a split hull. Gideon makes the call to run the river rather than lose days. Emotional beat: leadership under pressure, the price of survival beginning to show.

chapters.title: Leaking
chapters.summary: The boat takes water in the rapids; supplies are lost, including half the medical kit. Tomas accuses Gideon of repeating the old disaster's arrogance. Emotional beat: the crew's trust fracturing along old fault lines.

chapters.title: Stranger on the Bank
chapters.summary: Grounded and soaked, they encounter Yusuf, a lone fisherman-guide who knows the monsoon patterns. He offers shelter and passage upriver — for a price he won't name yet. Emotional beat: wary gratitude; pride swallowing hard.

chapters.title: Monsoon Walls
chapters.summary: Yusuf's POV. Rain closes the valley; the group shelters in his stilt house. He recognizes Gideon's name and carries his own history with the pass they seek. Emotional beat: two strangers discovering shared wounds.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Yusuf's price: Gideon must take him to the ice cave where his own son died, so he can bury something he left there. Gideon realizes the mountain collects everyone eventually. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged in honesty.

chapters.title: Dev's Signal Fire
chapters.summary: Bisi catches Dev transmitting their position via satellite messenger. Confronted, Dev confesses smugglers paid him for the route — but he's had a change of heart. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the fragile question of forgiveness.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Smugglers shadowing them fire warning shots across the river. The crew splits loads and pushes through a gorge at night, Yusuf piloting the patched boat. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce solidarity.

chapters.title: Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: They abandon the boat and climb. Altitude sickness fells Tomas; Gideon must choose between speed toward the cave and carrying him down. Emotional beat: the survival theme made flesh — who do you save, and what does it cost?

chapters.title: The Cave Below the Serac
chapters.summary: Gideon and Yusuf reach the ice cave. Inside: Emeka's remains, preserved, and beside them a brass compass engraved with her childhood nickname. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness — grief given a body at last.

chapters.title: Emeka's Last Miles
chapters.summary: A journal recovered with the body reveals Emeka survived four days, forgave his sister, and left the compass deliberately — inheritance as absolution. Gideon reads it aloud through tears. Emotional beat: catharsis; memory as both burden and gift.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Ambush
chapters.summary: Descending, they're ambushed at the moraine. Bisi is wounded covering the retreat; Dev redeems himself drawing the smugglers off. Emotional beat: climax of action — every character pays a price for another's survival.

chapters.title: Dry Season Running Out
chapters.summary: Wounded and short on food, they race the last pass before weather seals it. Gideon leads not by miles but by judgment, delegating, trusting. Emotional beat: the leader reborn — inheritance claimed, not fled.

chapters.title: Burial at the Pass
chapters.summary: At the summit cairn, Yusuf buries his son's keepsake; Gideon leaves Emeka's journal pages with him, keeping only the compass. Emotional beat: release — letting the mountain keep what belongs to it.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: They cross into Nepal as the first clear skies break. Bisi stabilizes; Dev turns himself in to authorities, naming the smugglers. Emotional beat: exhausted peace, the crew bound by what they endured.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Kathmandu. Gideon testifies, exposing the smuggling ring and clearing the record of the original disaster — Mara's evidence proving the fall wasn't her fault. Her blacklist dissolves. Emotional beat: vindication that feels quieter than expected.

chapters.title: True North
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Gideon's POV. Months later she guides a small group up an ordinary trail, compass in pocket, teaching a young porter to read weather. She measures life now in years after all. Emotional beat: resolution — survival's price paid, its inheritance accepted.
